[Thinking]
**Defining Core Inflation**

I've started with defining "Core Inflation". It's the CPI, less Food and Energy. The data source is the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). I'm focusing on the U.S. Core Inflation Rate year-over-year from January 2015 to December 2016. I am organizing this information in a Markdown table.
[/Thinking]

This table shows the Year-over-Year (YoY) U.S. Core Inflation Rate (Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items Less Food and Energy) from January 2015 through December 2016.

| Month | 2015 Core Inflation (YoY) | 2016 Core Inflation (YoY) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **January** | 1.6% | 2.2% |
| **February** | 1.7% | 2.3% |
| **March** | 1.8% | 2.2% |
| **April** | 1.8% | 2.1% |
| **May** | 1.7% | 2.2% |
| **June** | 1.8% | 2.3% |
| **July** | 1.8% | 2.2% |
| **August** | 1.8% | 2.3% |
| **September** | 1.9% | 2.2% |
| **October** | 1.9% | 2.1% |
| **November** | 2.0% | 2.1% |
| **December** | 2.1% | 2.2% |

***Source:** U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)*
